follow-up time: First 72 hours of life for 90% of infants with infections
exposure: Moderate and late preterm birth (32-36 weeks gestational age)
cohort: 771 moderate and late preterm infants consecutively admitted to a neonatal unit between June 2008 and November 2013
finding: Moderate and late preterm infants have a significantly increased risk of infection compared to term infants, with umbilical venous catheter insertion, antenatal corticosteroids, and cesarean section identified as potential risk factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section birth was identified as a potential risk factor for infection, with observed values very similar to expected values.
